Subject: Finova - Performance SLOs & Regional Routing - post-call recap

Hi Liam / Priya —

Thanks for the call today. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on so we can move to a short benchmark and finalize the MRP (mutual rollout plan):

1) Performance targets (please confirm):
- Latency: target p95 <= 250ms for short-turn prompts (~<256 tokens).
- First-byte streaming: require partial response streaming such that first byte reaches client within 300ms for streaming-enabled routes.
- Throughput: baseline 500 requests/sec sustained during peak windows.
- Concurrency: support for 200 concurrent user sessions (each session may stream).

2) Regional routing / residency:
- US & EU: EU data must remain in EU for EU customers (data residency).
- APAC: lower priority initially, but regional endpoints preferred in APAC for later expansion.
- Routing policy: prefer regional routing with automatic fallback to nearest compatible region; need confirmation on whether Finova requires strict region-only routing or is okay with geo-failover for availability.

3) Security/compliance notes:
- You flagged token-level logging and KV cache retention concerns — we will provide options to disable prefix caching and ensure no plaintext retention for PII/PHI.

Next steps we proposed on the call:
- Redwood to run a focused benchmark against production-like prompts (we'll need a representative prompt set + a test endpoint allowlist).
- Finova to confirm/resend the definitive SLO numbers and any network constraints (eg: egress IP allowlist, corporate proxy).
- Plan a 30-45 minute follow-up on Mon/Tue next week to review benchmark results and proposed routing/architecture.

Attached: SLO_matrix.xlsx (initial SLO mapping), mutual_action_plan.xlsx (proposed timeline).

Would you confirm the numbers above (latency / throughput / residency) and preferred time for next week?

Thanks,

Thanks Marissa — good write-up. A few clarifications from our side:

- Latency: p95 <= 250ms is correct for our customer-facing short prompts (login/authorization flows). For longer generation flows (>=1024 tokens) we expect throughput rather than single-request p95 guarantees; provide guidance on tail behavior there.
- Streaming: yes, streaming is mandatory for the customer-facing flows. We expect the first byte to arrive <300ms and then steady token pacing thereafter.
- Throughput & concurrency: 500 req/s sustained is our target for regional peaks; concurrency 200 sessions is correct. We may need short bursts up to ~750 req/s for special events (holiday spikes).
- Regional routing / residency: EU data must remain in EU by default — no cross-border storage. For availability, we are open to geo-failover only if data residency boundaries are honored (i.e., failover that reads/writes data outside EU is not permitted).

Security ask: please ensure caching can be disabled per-route and that any logs containing model inputs/outputs can be redacted or routed to our S3 with encryption keys we control (KMS). Also attaching our security questionnaire (security-questionnaire.pdf).

We can do the follow-up on Tue 2026-03-10 at 10:00 AM GMT if that works for your team.

-Liam

Hi all — posting a quick technical answer to the items Liam flagged and suggesting a test plan.

1) Latency & streaming:
- For p95 <=250ms on short prompts we'll recommend a smaller, low-latency model variant pinned to regional endpoints (quantized float16 + optimized kernels).
- Streaming first-byte <300ms is achievable with our streaming pipeline; we'll instrument first-byte latency in the benchmark (we measure TTFB and steady-state token latency separately).

2) Throughput & concurrency:
- 500 req/s sustained with 200 concurrent sessions is within Dedicated pool capacity. For bursty spikes to 750 req/s we recommend enabling burst capacity (reserve headroom or use autoscale rules).

3) Regional routing & residency:
- We can deploy region-specific endpoint clusters (EU-only) to satisfy residency. Routing policies can be configured to be strict region-only (no cross-border failover) or region-preferred with opt-in failover. For compliance, we'll default to strict EU-only reads/writes unless you sign off on geo-failover policy.

4) Caching & logs:
- Per-route cache disable is supported; we can also encrypt and forward logs to your S3 with customer-managed KMS. We will include a config profile for no-input retention.

5) Proposed quick benchmark (what we need from Finova):
- Representative prompt set (10-20 prompts across short/long flows)
- Allowlist IPs for our benchmark harness and a short-lived API key
- Desired concurrency pattern (ramp profile) and target sustained window (e.g., 10 minutes at 500 req/s)

I'll spin up an initial benchmark plan and share a short runbook (ETA: Mon 2026-03-09). If the team confirms the Tue 2026-03-10 10:00 AM GMT call, we'll run an initial benchmark the day prior (Mon) and present results on Tue.
